newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends up slightly, but resistance holds.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends up slightly, but resistance holds.

text.p: CSCE coffee ended marginally firmer Wednesday amid light speculative and commercial buying, but failed to regain highs set early in the day, dealers said.

The arabica market drifted in the plus column throughout the session, topping out early on at a one-week peak of 107.25. Buy stops were thought to be well-placed above that level, but several bids to challenge resistance met with little success.
Front-month December gained 0.45 cent per lb to settle at 106.45 cents after ranging from 106 to 107.25. The deferred contracts rose 0.50 to 1.65.
The day's volume was estimated at 4,306 lots.
Traders said selling pressure by origins appeared to have thinned out in recent days, allowing the market to find some stability in the 103-109 cent range.
The sense that the market may have hit a temporary floor has touched off steady buying from European and U.S. end-users, said Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes.
But she cautioned that with more coffee on the way from key producing countries, the positive momentum was likely to be short-lived.
"I don't think (coffee) has hit its peak, but I wouldn't expect a lot more follow-through," she said.
Technically, dealers noted stiff resistance in the 108.50-109 cent range, while major support was identified at 101.50 cents.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
